scenes.line1: How do you track data changes?
scenes.say: How do you keep your ETL or ELT pipelines efficient when data keeps changing? What’s a watermark or change data capture?

scenes.label: Watermark
scenes.sub: A marker like a timestamp or ID to track the latest processed data.
scenes.say: A watermark is just a marker, like a timestamp or an ID, that tracks the latest data your pipeline has processed.
Change data capture means you only grab the inserts, updates, and deletes since your last run. No need to reprocess everything.

scenes.title: Using a Watermark
scenes.say: For example, you store the highest updated time from your last run, then query for anything newer next time.

scenes.question: Where should you store watermarks?
scenes.right: Always persist watermarks in a durable store so you never lose your place if your pipeline restarts.
scenes.say: Here’s a common mistake: storing watermarks in memory. Always keep them in a durable place so you can recover after a restart.
